paper.title: Mapping the AI Landscape in Food Science and Engineering: A Bibliometric Analysis Enhanced with Interactive Digital Tools and Company Case Studies

evidence.paraphrase: Bibliometric review of AI in food science, with an interactive dashboard over a curated dataset of review articles and custom LLM tools for literature interrogation.
User-driven exploration of a curated literature set is present, but there is no treatment of overrides, provenance, explainable selection or feedback-loop safeguards.

reviews.rationale: The paper offers an interactive literature-exploration tool as a by-product of a domain review, which touches human-in-the-loop curation only descriptively. It does not evaluate or govern curation decisions, so it is too generic for the role; a boundary call.

paper.title: Explainable artificial intelligence in the talent recruitment process-a literature review

evidence.paraphrase: Literature review of explainable AI (LIME, SHAP, knowledge graphs) across the talent-recruitment process.
'Person-job recommendation' and 'traceability' are HR-domain uses, not scholarly curation.

reviews.rationale: Explainability in recruitment decisions does not concern literature curation or scholarly evidence selection; the match is through XAI and recommendation vocabulary. Out of scope.

paper.title: Governing Adaptive News Curation: Sequential Optimization, Cumulative Exposure Allocation, and Societal Accountability

evidence.paraphrase: Conceptualises adaptive news curation as decision functions linked by a feedback and optimisation layer, with human-review delay as a dimension of autonomy.
Defines cumulative exposure allocation with concentration, breadth, repetition, persistence and disparity measures, and shifts evaluation to patterns produced by a policy over time.
The domain is news, not scholarly literature, and the contribution is conceptual without empirical evaluation.

reviews.rationale: The paper directly theorises feedback loops, exposure concentration and accountability in repeated adaptive curation, which closely mirrors the role's concern with safeguards against feedback loops and the project's stateful-selection framing. Because it is about news rather than scholarly curation, it serves as a bridging conceptual reference rather than direct evidence.

paper.title: Cyborg Workflows Merging Human Judgment and Agentic AI for Digital Media Transformation

evidence.paraphrase: Preprint proposing 'cyborg workflows' combining human judgment and agentic AI for digital media production, content generation and news curation.
Reports broad efficiency gains (3x throughput, 25-60% improvements) without specifying literature curation, provenance or override mechanisms.

reviews.rationale: The paper is a general human-AI media-workflow framework and does not address scholarly literature curation; its claims are broad and unspecific in the abstract. Out of scope under the generic-agent exclusion.

paper.title: A comprehensive taxonomy for explainable artificial intelligence: a systematic survey of surveys on methods and concepts

evidence.paraphrase: Survey of over 50 XAI surveys producing a unified taxonomy of explanation methods, metrics and traits.
Explainability is treated for ML methods in general, not for literature selection or curation.

reviews.rationale: A general XAI taxonomy is too broad to evidence explainable or human-controlled literature curation. Out of scope for this role.
